newsitem.title: GERMANY: German govt cash position deeper in the red - Buba.
newsitem.headline: German govt cash position deeper in the red - Buba.

text.p: The federal German government's cash position slipped further into the red in November as traditional payments of "Christmas money" climbed from the year before, the Bundesbank said.
The central bank said in its report for January the federal cash deficit in November climbed to 15.4 billion marks from nearly 12 billion marks during the same month in 1995.
That pushed the federal cash deficit for the year through November to nearly 84 billion marks, up from 38.39 billion marks during the same period a year earlier.
Cash expenditures during the first 11 months of 1996 were up 13.5 percent to 544.13 billion marks while cash income was up only 4.3 percent to 460.42 billion marks.
To finance the deficit, the Bundesbank has increased its capital market debt to 72.52 billion marks from 33.30 billion marks for the first 11 months of the year.
Money market debt increased to 9.80 billion marks from 1.40 billion marks during the period.
Total borrowing by central, regional and local authorities between January and November climbed to 117.9 billion marks from 79.7 billion marks during the same period in 1995.

The bulk of the debt taken during the first 11 months was raised by the federal government with 82.3 billion marks. State authorities took 46.6 billion marks and local governments borrowed 6.9 billion marks.
In December, the federal government's gross borrowing totalled 15 billion marks.
